results.fact: Total gain vs trailhead and summit elevations
results.evidence: The contradiction is real (4,300 ft pullout to 8,350 ft summit cannot be 2,850 ft of gain). No source states a car-to-car gain for this route; related figures are ~3,500 ft to Burgundy Col (Chianti trip report) and 4,500 ft for Silver Star via the same approach, which cannot be transferred to this route under the no-arithmetic rule.

Sources disagree on the approach length: one trip report gives under 5 miles to Burgundy Col, another logged 5.68 miles round trip to the Silver Star summit via the same col, implying well under 3 miles one way. No source gives a one-way figure for Chablis, so neither dist_km (2.8 mi) nor the summit pin's 4 mi could be settled.

results.evidence: The route is published as II 5.6 (Hieb-Maki 1952). The summit block shared with the east-face routes is given as 5.7 in Rebel Yell pitch lists, and a 1989 note calls the finish from the notch the 'normal route' with no separate grade. No two sources settle whether the North Face's summit move is 5.6 or 5.7.

results.correct_value: Party reached the Chianti-Pernod notch via 500 ft of rock from the east, rappelled 250 ft down the west face, then followed a loose gully to the Chianti-Burgundy notch
results.evidence: The original account says the party climbed moraine and ice to the eastern walls, climbed 500 ft to the notch between Chianti and Pernod, rappelled 250 ft on the west face and followed a loose gully to the Chianti-Burgundy notch - matching approach_variants, not beta/overview. Every other page found restates that single account, so only one independent source; no patch written.

A trip report records 4 double-rope rappels on two 60 m ropes; another page confirms the descent rappels the route on fixed anchors with two ropes. Row fields rappels, beta, descent_text, pro_tips, pitch_detail[6], rappel_detail and approach_variants all say 4; the itinerary's ~7 is the outlier.

A trip report and a guide service both describe seven pitches; another database lists 6 (counting the start options differently), which the overview's 6-to-7 note already covers. The row's pitches column and pitch table say 7.

One trip report gives under 5 miles and 3,500 ft to the col; another logged 5.68 miles round trip to Silver Star's summit via the same col, which implies under ~3 miles one way to the col. The sources disagree, so neither 'just under 5 miles' nor 3.9 mi is settled.
